root_cause.text: The iris V4L2 vb2 stop-streaming path incorrectly skipped buffer teardown when `inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR`, so `iris_vb2_stop_streaming()` failed to complete/return queued buffers and could leave cleanup incomplete in the media/firmware state machine.
root_cause.evidence: The reverted code added `if (inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR) goto exit;` in `drivers/media/platform/qcom/iris/iris_vb2.c`, which bypassed the normal stop-streaming flow; the patch description says this caused “Buffers were not returned to vb2” and that stop_streaming was skipped during cleanup for sessions that had already transitioned to `IRIS_INST_ERROR`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow stop_streaming to run its cleanup path even when the Iris instance is in the error state.
intent_record.what: In iris_vb2_stop_streaming(), the early check for `inst->state == IRIS_INST_ERROR` and its `goto exit;` path were removed under `mutex_lock(&inst->lock);`.
intent_record.how: After this change, `stop_streaming()` will continue executing its normal cleanup path even when the instance is already in the error state, instead of returning immediately. This allows streaming shutdown and associated resource cleanup to proceed in error conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always complete queued buffers with error on streaming stop, while only transitioning the instance to error when stop streaming fails.
intent_record.what: The call to `iris_helper_buffers_done(inst, q->type, VB2_BUF_STATE_ERROR);` was moved out of the `if (ret)` block so it now executes unconditionally in the `exit:` path, while the `iris_inst_change_state(inst, IRIS_INST_ERROR);` call remains conditional on `ret`.
intent_record.how: On stream stop, all buffers are now marked done with error regardless of whether `ret` is set, ensuring queued buffers are always completed and released; only the instance error state is still entered when an actual error occurred.
